[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone good afternoon, thanks for carving time. Mic check, can you hear me?
[00:06] Michael: Yep loud and clear, thanks Alex.
[00:10] Priya: All good here.
[00:12] Tom: Yup.
[00:15] Alex: Cool, so agenda — quick pipeline review, call out blockers, any tech asks for POCs, and define next steps. Sara's gonna run through the technical asks after I hit the top deals.
[00:26] Priya: Sounds good.
[00:30] Alex: Ok first up Acorn, where Sable has an intro. Michael, whats the status there?
[00:35] Michael: Acorn's in discovery, they care a lot about latency and cost, also data residency — they're based in EU. They asked for a canary on private deployment or dedicated.
[00:45] Sara: Right, and just to flag, for EU residency we can do Redwood Private in a VPC region or dedicated capacity pinned to EU zone. There's some perf tradeoffs when you go private vs hosted but we can quantify.
[00:58] Tom: Do we know what SLA they'll need? They mentioned 99.9 earlier but not formally.
[01:04] Michael: Yeah 99.9 is the ask, also SOC2 + SSO.
[01:09] Alex: Good. On the commercial side we should make sure lead registration is clear. Priya, do you have the partner comp appendix?
[01:16] Priya: I have the draft, but need to confirm on our end — wondering about co-sell discount thresholds, is Redwood okay with a standard partner discount for co-sell motions?
[01:25] Alex: We can support partner discounts for committed Dedicated deals, need to align with RevOps. I'll send the template.
[01:32] Priya: Cool.
[01:35] Sara: Quick tech note on Acorn — if they're sensitive on PII, we recommend either private deployment with customer-managed KMS or dedicated with strict retention rules. Our KV cache and prefix caching can be tuned so we don't persist unwanted contexts.
[01:48] Michael: Good. Can you do a trial where we route EU traffic to a dedicated pool and fall back to hosted? They like the graceful degradation idea.
[01:56] Sara: Yeah that's doable — smart routing supports region+tier fallback. We'll need to size the dedicated pool for peak concurrent users, otherwise you'll see latency increases.
[02:06] Alex: Ok next deal — Meridian, which is further along. Tom, update?
[02:10] Tom: Meridian's on a demo next week; they want end-to-end latency numbers with batching enabled. Also they asked about quantization options because they care about unit cost and token throughput.
[02:21] Sara: For quantization (Q4 or Q8 depending on model) we can provide perf profiles. Important note: quantization can change model quality slightly; we should pair with eval prompts. Redwood Optimize can suggest the config.
[02:35] Alex: Are they considering on-prem vs cloud?
[02:37] Tom: They prefer cloud but need private networking — basically VPC peering.
[02:42] Sara: VPC/private plane with SAML SSO + audit logs is straightforward. We'll share our SOC2 and ISO docs.
[02:49] Michael: Speaking of docs, can you share the security pack and any certs? I need to pass them to Meridian's procurement.
[02:56] Alex: Yes I'll drop the security one-pager and the full pack.
[03:00] Priya: For joint GTM, we should align on who runs the executive brief — Sable typically runs the initial exec plaster, Redwood does the deep technical.
[03:09] Alex: Makes sense. We'll do joint materials.

[03:15] — small pause / audio shuffling —

[03:30] Alex: Sara, can you walk through the Acorn POC ask — what do you need from Sable and from the customer?
[03:36] Sara: Sure. From Sable: stakeholder intros and a clear list of success metrics — e.g., p99 latency target, tokens per sec, cost per 1k tokens target. From customer: sample traffic patterns, sample prompt sets (redacted), and whether they need EU-only data flows. On our side we can spin a dedicated pool in EU and run a 2-week benchmark. We'll also record subtleties like KV cache hit rates and batch windows.
[03:58] Michael: They can provide sample prompts, but maybe sanitized.
[04:02] Sara: That's fine. Sanitized is fine; we can still run perf and quality evals.
[04:06] Tom: For the benchmark what input size distribution should we use? Meridian previously used short query (8–32 tokens) vs long chat sessions.
[04:15] Sara: We'll want both. For Acorn I'd expect higher context sizes, so include 512+ tokens scenarios. Also measure cold start p95/p99.
[04:24] Alex: Good. On contracts — do we need an MSA or can we use Sable's template?
[04:29] Priya: Sable typically uses a partner-led engagement and then passes Redwood's T&Cs. We need a simple co-sell agreement and an allocation doc.
[04:37] Alex: I'll work with legal to produce a short co-sell addendum.

[04:42] [05:00] Michael: Ok other pipeline items: Zephyr — low touch, small deal. Should we drop engineering time or make it a hosted paid pilot?
[05:10] Sara: For low-touch, hosted trial with usage cap is easiest, keep a small sandbox. No special infra.
[05:15] Tom: That saves cycles.

[05:20] Alex: Any blockers from Redwood side to note? Sara?
[05:23] Sara: Not really blockers, more resource scheduling — if both Acorn and Meridian want dedicated pools in the same week we'll need cross-team coordination. Might need to stagger POCs by a week.
[05:33] Alex: Noted. I'll add to the pipeline sheet.

[05:38] Priya: One ask on partner reporting — can Redwood provide a weekly co-sell pipeline export (CSV) that has expected close dates, ARR, and deal stage? Our RevOps needs that for forecasting.
[05:49] Alex: We can provide an automated export; I'll ask ops to create a shared Google Sheet with a push.

[06:00] Michael: On the tech objections — some customers ask why not run models on Vertex or Anthropic — any quick messaging?
[06:08] Alex: We position Redwood as inference-first: predictable economics and unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private. Also our Optimize tooling and rollout controls (canary/A-B + automatic fallback) are differentiators.
[06:20] Sara: Technically, our kernel selection and KV cache optimizations give better steady-state throughput for some architectures, which reduces unit costs for high-throughput apps. But we try to avoid overselling — mention benchmarks and offer to run a direct comparison.
[06:33] Tom: Good. Can we provide a short slide that compares Redwood vs cloud providers on latency/cost?
[06:39] Alex: Yes, I'll attach a two-page benchmark summary.

[06:45] [08:12] Priya: Question — what about revenue recognition splits and referral fees? Financial ops need clarity.
[08:18] Alex: That's mainly commercial but typical co-sell can be referral fee or carveout. I'll propose 10% referral for net new Acorn-scale deals, but final numbers depend on Redwood RevOps signoff.
[08:30] Priya: Ok flagged.

[08:35] Michael: For the Acorn POC, timeline wise can Redwood deliver a dedicated EU pool in two weeks?
[08:42] Sara: Two weeks is aggressive but possible if we prioritize. Need lead time to provision infra and get customer networking (VPC peering). If Sable can coordinate with Acorn's infra team we'll hit it.
[08:52] Alex: Michael can you confirm Acorn infra contact?
[08:55] Michael: Yes, I'll send an intro after the call.

[09:00] Tom: Any security red flags we should prepare for?
[09:03] Sara: They may ask for SOC2, penetration test summary, and KMS integration details. We'll share our SOC2 summary and KMS integration doc. For private deployments we can support customer-managed KMS.
[09:14] Priya: Great.

[09:20] Alex: Ok shifting to playbook — we should define a simple co-sell checklist: 1) lead registration + brief, 2) joint intro + exec one-pager, 3) technical scoping, 4) pilot/POC, 5) contract + handoff. Thoughts?
[09:36] Michael: That's clean. Could add milestone for executive alignment prior to pilot start.
[09:40] Alex: Good call.

[09:45] Sara: I'll draft a one-page checklist and share.

[12:20] Alex: Can we set concrete dates now? Michael said intros to Acorn by 10/13, Sara bench by 10/18, co-sell sheet by 10/12. Any objections?
